statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits at 14 of 100 in the low band, eleven points below the 25 block threshold, while stress remains extreme at 86 and confidence is high at 89.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold and the deterministic mapping therefore returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window covers the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC on 11 September and the first cash-open hour that follows, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: Ninety minutes of post-reopen trade confirm the benign read: NQ holds 29,107.00, down 0.10% inside a 59-point band, Oracle's after-hours quote is steady at +4.28% rather than extending, and tail eases to 14 while a 4.944% ten-year and crude above $100 keep stress at 86.
body:
The checkpoint that dominated the previous two assessments is now fully resolved. CME equity futures have been open for roughly ninety minutes since the 22:00 UTC maintenance halt, and NQ trades 29,107.00, down 28.25 points or 0.10% against the 29,135.25 pause reference, inside a band of 29,098.75 to 29,157.50. That is a 59-point range, about 0.20%, with no gap and no directional leg. Price has drifted toward the lower half of that band rather than holding an extreme, and the move has been gradual across the full session rather than an impulse. Tail eases a further point to 14.

The single-name transmission has now been measured over a full hour rather than a twenty-minute sample. Oracle published fiscal first-quarter results at 20:10 UTC: total revenue of $19.3 billion, up 30%, total cloud revenue of $11.6 billion, up 62%, cloud infrastructure revenue of $7.4 billion, up 121%, cloud applications revenue of $4.2 billion, up 10%, non-GAAP earnings of $1.92 per share against $1.74 expected, GAAP earnings of $1.56, and remaining performance obligations of $664 billion, an increase of $209 billion year over year. Second-quarter revenue growth was guided to 30% to 34% in constant currency with non-GAAP earnings of $1.83 to $1.91, and fiscal 2027 was guided to at least $90 billion of revenue and $8.10 of non-GAAP earnings per share. Against a regular session that closed down 5.38% at $152.94, the shares were quoted at $159.49 at 23:26 UTC, up 4.28%. An hour earlier the same quote stood at $159.41, up 4.23%. An after-hours impulse that peaked near 7%, faded, and has since held flat for an hour is settled rather than extending, and a settled impulse is the opposite of the path this framework treats as dangerous.

The index structure behind it is unchanged and remains the reason tail is low. Cash NAS100 closed at 29,103.51, down 318.04 points or 1.08%, with the entire session contained inside a 212-point band between 29,038.22 and 29,250.41. The opening-auction low was set in the first hour and never revisited, and the path offered retracement in both directions throughout. The broader tape closed lower for a fourth consecutive session, with the S&P 500 down 0.58% at 7,591.70, the Dow down 316.56 points at 52,064.10 and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.65% at 26,081.73. Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion for long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach, not the size of a decline. A four-day drift lower in which every session has offered two-way trade does not meet that description.

What holds stress in the extreme band is the macro and cross-asset backdrop. The ten-year Treasury yield settled at 4.944%, up 10.7 basis points and near the top of a 4.879 to 4.952 range, its highest since 2023. The two-year is at 4.586%, a 52-week high, and the thirty-year reached about 5.36%, the highest since 2007, carrying the thirty-year mortgage rate to 7.07%. That is a bear steepening of the whole curve. Crude remains elevated but is no longer extending: WTI trades $103.68, up 1.17% against the $102.48 settlement, inside an evening range of $103.62 to $104.44, after settlements of $102.48 and $107.63 that were the highest closes since 19 May. Both benchmarks are up more than 75% year to date. The driver is an unresolved Persian Gulf conflict in which Iran has signalled an exclusion zone running from the U.S. naval blockade line through the Strait of Hormuz. VIX closed at 17.84, up 8.38%, at the top of its 16.29 to 18.17 range. Gold fell 1.2% on the day, which points to a real-rate and energy repricing rather than a broad flight to safety. August producer prices, published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics at 12:30 UTC, rose 0.4% month over month and 5.4% year over year. Latest-session sector context showed semiconductors weaker than the broader index.

The forward window is shaped by one scheduled event. The August consumer price report is released at 12:30 UTC on 11 September, confirmed against the Bureau of Labor Statistics release schedule, and it is the last inflation reading before the FOMC decision on 16 September. Published consensus centres near 3.3% to 3.4% headline year over year with core near 2.4%. Conditional tail peaks at 23 in that slot and holds 23 at 13:00 UTC where post-release discovery overlaps the 13:30 UTC cash open, then eases to 20 at the University of Michigan release. All three map to WATCH and none reaches the block threshold of 25, because no post-release price path is observed at publication time and, under this framework, surprise magnitude and forecast dispersion widen uncertainty before they raise tail. What would raise tail is observable rather than hypothetical: an opening auction that extends without meaningful retracement, repeated extension after failed pullbacks, or price holding near session extremes. The window then closes into the weekly CME futures close at 21:00 UTC on 11 September, after which no venue is open until Sunday at 22:00 UTC.

Confidence rises to 89. The futures sample is now roughly ninety minutes rather than twenty, the Oracle after-hours reaction has been observed across a full hour and has stabilised, and current verified levels are in hand across the index, futures, the two-year, ten-year and thirty-year, crude, volatility, the published producer price data, the Oracle actuals and guidance, and the confirmed release calendar. The remaining caveats are narrow and stated: overnight Globex liquidity is thin, and no post-CPI price path can exist at publication time.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 23:00 UTC on 9 September to 22:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 9 and holds a tight 8 to 11 band through the U.S. overnight, the Asian session and the European morning, with the dominant mode recorded as mixed throughout. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and a 24 peak at 13:00 UTC covering post-release discovery and the cash open. Those two slots are the only ones in the window that mapped to WATCH. The final nine slots record the decay back into range and then a modest rebuild: 17, 14, then 16 as yields and crude extended, 15, 16, 17 into the final cash hour, 19 at 20:00 UTC as Oracle's results landed after the close, 18 at 21:00 UTC across the CME maintenance halt, and 15 at 22:00 UTC once the reopen resolved that checkpoint without a gap. Stress never left the extreme band, running 80 to 87 throughout. That is the defining feature of the window: a persistently difficult environment in which the observed price path nevertheless kept offering retracement.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with roughly ninety minutes of observed post-reopen trade on 10 September and ends inside the CME weekend closure on 11 September. Conditional tail starts at 14, eases to 13 through the Oracle conference-call hour and the Tokyo open, and settles at a 12 floor across the thinnest Asian and pre-European hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled. From the European pre-market it rebuilds gradually, 13 through 14, reaching 15 and then 16 in the final full hour before the release as pre-event liquidity thins. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report and 23 again at 13:00 UTC where post-release discovery overlaps the 13:30 UTC cash open, then 20 at the University of Michigan release; all three map to WATCH and none reaches the block threshold, since no post-release price path is observed. The path then eases to 18, 16, 15 and 15 through the New York afternoon before ticking to 16 in the power hour and 17 at the cash close, as pre-weekend adjustment concentrates into a week that has closed lower four sessions running with an unresolved Persian Gulf conflict carrying across the weekend. The last two slots fall inside the weekly CME closure from 21:00 UTC, where no live price path can form, and settle at 14 and 13. Stress stays in the extreme band throughout, peaking at 90 around the release, and confidence declines from 89 to 60 with distance from observed evidence.
